note: Behaviour fixtures, grouped by the language PAIR they run under. kbfix works on two languages at a time, so each case is only meaningful against a stated pair: `ghbdtn` reads as привет under en-ru and is left alone under en-he, and both are correct. `expect: null` means the detector must abstain. Add a case here whenever a miss or a false positive bites you; --self-test is the regression gate.

en-es.why: the ONLY kind of Spanish mistype there is: the ñ key is where ; sits on a US board, so the letters are all fine and one punctuation mark is wrong
pequeño keeps its missing tilde: an accented vowel is a dead-key sequence and is not recoverable, only ñ is
correctly typed Spanish. Transposing it changes NOTHING, so there is no evidence of a mistake. Without that guard every Spanish sentence would be flagged as mistyped English
correctly typed Spanish, unchanged by transposition
a trailing semicolon is not a glued letter; code must survive a Spanish layout being installed
semicolons followed by spaces, not wedged inside words
shell separator, not a lost ñ

en-he.why: ground truth: a real mistyped message, confirmed by the person who typed it
punctuation shifts too: ' arrives as a comma
the reverse direction, and a word no stopword list contains: this is what the bigram channel exists for
leading comma is the ' key; two real Hebrew words
slashes and dots sit inside words but do not become letters on any layout, so they are not evidence

en-he.input: אני צריך לבדוק את הקובץ הזה
can you check the hook please

en-he.why: near-gibberish both ways, no call is safe
two letters: both real Hebrew ('if') and layout-typed 'to'
digits are identical in both layouts and carry no direction
mixed script: half-decoding is worse than not decoding

en-ru.why: Russian typed with English selected, the third layout's basic case
the comma key is a Cyrillic letter, so punctuation carries signal here too
Russian is bicameral and nothing is dropped, so unlike Hebrew the capital SURVIVES
